comments.text: the cockpit screen

Draws the 3D view into the view buffer: a new picture when bit 2 of $8920 asks for one, the last one again when bit 3 of $8921 does. On the tape the first two bytes are JR $6B12, a jump to itself: the game hangs on its first call here unless the security question was answered, which writes $DD and $E5 (PUSH IX) over them ($CBD8, $CCE8). A new picture bounds what can be seen (bound_view_box), builds the view matrix (make_view_matrix) and the multiply routines for it (make_multipliers), empties the sensor list, then puts every object of the area ($8864, $8863 of them) and the player's own objects at $87A5 ($890F of them) through draw_object_list, sorts what was queued (sort_faces) and draws it (draw_faces). The record that $8BF3 points to takes the frame count $8A65 at the start (+1), after the objects (+2) and after the sort (+3).
The sensor list starts empty: $8A24 counts it, $8A62 is where the next record goes.
No new picture: the last one again only when bit 3 of $8921 is set.

Draws A objects from the list at IX, each record as long as its byte +8 says. An object is skipped when its type (the low nibble of +0) is 0, when bit 6 (hidden) is set, or when it lies wholly outside the box bound_view_box made: on each axis its position (+1 to +3, in units of 64) must be no more than the first limit of the pair at $88E5 and its far side (position plus size, +4 to +6) no less than the second, each by the sign of the byte difference. A sensor (type 2) is neither culled nor tested for hidden here. A drawn object's two corners go to the object buffer ($8BDE) as six words, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1, each scaled by 64 and taken from the player ($8762); bits 0 to 5 of $5E62 record, for each, whether it is on the far side of the player (the low corner above zero, the high corner below). Then the type picks the drawer: 1 a cuboid (draw_cuboid), 2 a sensor (draw_sensor), 3 a rectangle (draw_rectangle), 4 to 9 the pyramids and prisms (draw_pyramid), 10 and up the lines and flat polygons (draw_polygon), with the object's id (+7) in $8916 and its type in $5E61.
The corners: for x, y and z in turn, position x 64 less the player's, then plus size x 64, each a word.
On to the next record: +8 is its length.

Works out the part of the area's box that can be in view, so that draw_object_list can skip what lies outside it. The four corners of the view are the heading ($876C) and the pitch ($876D) each turned by $88D7 either way, in the game's 72 steps to the circle (5 degrees each); each corner falls in one of eight octants, numbered 1 to 8 here, and the octant decides which limits of the area's own box ($88DF-$88E4) bound the view on that side. They go to $88E5-$88EA, a pair for each axis, the upper limit first. An axis no corner bounded keeps $FF, and one of its pair is set from the player's position ($8762, $8764, $8766, x 4, the high byte): the upper one above it, or else the lower one at it.
The octant: the pitch picks 1, 3, 5 or 7 by its quarter, the heading adds 1, 5, 4 or nothing by its own, wrapping past 8.
The axes no corner bounded, from the player's position.

Writes a multiply routine for each of the nine entries of the view matrix ($5E55, signed bytes, $40 = 1.0) into the buffer that $8A97 points to, and its address into the table at $8A83, row by row. Each multiplies DE by the entry's magnitude with shifts and adds unrolled for its own bits: LD HL,0 / XOR A / LD C,0 or $FF (the entry's sign), then from the top set bit ADD HL,DE / ADC A,0 where a bit is set and ADD HL,HL / RLA between, ending JP $795E. An entry of 0 is JP $7981 alone. So the vertices are turned at a fixed cost for each entry, with no multiply loop. The buffer is the view buffer itself, cleared and drawn over once the vertices are turned.
A 3 x 3 identity matrix in the game's scale, $40 = 1.0, which make_view_matrix starts each rotation from.

Builds the view matrix at $5E55 from the player's angles, each a step of 5 degrees (0 to 71): the identity, then a rotation by the pitch ($876D), the heading ($876C) and the roll ($876E) in turn, each built at $5E4C from the sine and the cosine that the angle picks in the table at $8E78 (two bytes an angle, the sine first) and multiplied in by mul_matrix; an angle of 0 is skipped. Last comes a scaling, the diagonal $88D2-$88D4. Then it points the object buffer ($8BDE), the face list ($8BDC) and the draw list ($8BE0) at the buffers that $8A9B, $8A99 and $8A9D name, and clears the draw list's count ($8918) and the count of faces that fill the view ($8A6A).

Draws a cuboid (object type 1). Its eight corners are made from the two in the object buffer into the vertex list at $5E63, three words each, and transform_vertices turns them through the view. If any can be in view ($5E5F), the faces the player can see are chosen: for each axis the side bits in $5E62 say whether the low face or the high face faces the player, and that face takes its colour from a nibble of the object's colour bytes (+9 to +11, the low nibble for the low face); a face the player cannot see, or of colour 0, gets 0, which the face drawers skip. The six colours go to the face list at $8961, six bytes apart, and the faces are drawn by draw_face_list, or by clip_face_list when $5E5E says some corner is outside a clip plane.

Draws a pyramid or a prism, object types 4 to 9: one face the full size of the object, and an opposite face whose extent across the object is set by four more bytes of its record, +12 to +15, each in units of 64 (to $5EDC-$5EE2 as words). Types 4 and 5 point along x, one way and the other, 6 and 7 along y, 8 and 9 along z: each fills the eight corners at $5E63 from the object buffer with the inner face's offsets added on its own axes. The face list follows the shape of that inner face: $8986 (five faces) when it shrinks to a point, $89A1 or $89BE (six) when it is a line one way or the other, $89DB (eight) when it is a rectangle; its vertex count goes to $8A7F. After transform_vertices, if any corner can be in view, the faces of the list take their colours from the object's nibbles in turn (+9 on, the low nibble first), and are drawn with only the faces whose corners go one way round ($5E60 = 1) by draw_face_list, or clip_face_list when $5E5E is set.
Which face list: +12 against +14, and +13 against +15.
The four offsets of the inner face, times 64, to $5EDC.
Turn the corners, then give each face of the list its colour.

Draws a line or a flat polygon, object types 10 to 14: 2 to 6 corners (the type less 8, to $8A7F), each three bytes from +10 of the record, in units of 64, taken from the player's position into the vertex list at $5E63. After transform_vertices, if any can be in view, the one face at $8A00 is set up with its corner count: a line takes the low nibble of +9 as its colour ($5E60 = 0), and a polygon takes colour 1 with the whole byte +9 in $8917, its two nibbles the colours of its two sides ($5E60 = 2, the side seen picked by which way round its corners go). Drawn by draw_face_list, or clip_face_list when $5E5E is set.

Draws a rectangle, object type 3: a cuboid with one size 0. Its four corners come from the object buffer into $5E63; the flat axis is x if the size +4 is 0, else y if +5 is, else z, and B records it as 1, 2 or 3. After transform_vertices, if any corner can be in view, the side of the flat axis the player is on ($5E62) picks the colour: the low nibble of +9 when the player is beyond the low corner, the high nibble otherwise; a side of colour 0 is not drawn. One face of four corners at $8A00, drawn by draw_face_list, or clip_face_list when $5E5E is set.

Handles a sensor (object type 2). Every sensor of the area gets a 6-byte record in the sensor list at ($8A62), which draw_view starts empty and counts in $8A24: its id (+7), its range byte (+10), and a state at +3: 0 when it is hidden, when the player is on none of the sides it watches (the side bits $5E62 against its mask, +13) or when the player is out of its reach; 2 when it is in reach but not on the screen; and 1 when it is, with +4 and +5 then its point on the screen. Reach is |x| + |y| + |z| from the player to the sensor's corner, against the word +11. A sensor in reach is drawn as a line of two points at its corner, a dot ($8A09, colour the low nibble of +9), by draw_face_list.

Sorts the draw list for the painter's method: $8918 entries at ($8A9D), four bytes each, the last two pointing at the corners of the entry's object (x, y, z, each a low and a high word, from the player). Each pass compares every pair of neighbours. Axis by axis where their extents do not overlap, the side of the player each is on decides which is in front (two bits an axis in $5EE4); a pair is left as it is only when no axis says the first is nearer and at least one says it is farther, and is swapped otherwise. Passes repeat while any pass swapped ($5EE5), one fewer each time than there are entries.

Draws the sorted draw list ($8918 entries at ($8A9D)) into the view buffer, farthest first. Each entry points at an object's faces: its id, a count (bit 7 set when a face fills the whole view, the low seven bits the number of faces), then each face as a byte, its colour in the high nibble ($8917) and its corner count in the low ($8A7F), and its corners, two bytes each. A face of two corners is a line (prepare_line), any other a polygon (prepare_polygon); either is then filled into the buffer by fill_face. With $889F set the buffer ($8A95, 2,704 bytes) is cleared first; when $8A6A faces fill the view, drawing starts from the last of them and nothing is cleared.

Multiplies the rotation at $5E4C by the view matrix at $5E55, R x V, both 3 x 3 signed bytes with $40 = 1.0, into $5E55: each of the nine sums of three products (mul_s8) is a word at $5EEB, then divided by 64, rounding up on the top bit shifted out, and kept as a byte. The low bytes of the words are left shifted in place.

Turns the $8A7F vertices at $5E63 (three words each) through the view matrix into $5E9F (three words each, cleared first): each output coordinate is the sum of the three products of an input coordinate and a matrix entry, made by the routine make_multipliers wrote for that entry (the table at $8A83), whose result comes back through $795E. The input is made positive first and B remembers its sign. $5F01 and $5EFF follow the input and the output.

Where every generated multiply routine returns: A:H:L is |input| x |entry|; times 4 with the top two bytes kept it is the product divided by 64, truncated. The sign of the input (B) against the entry's (C) negates it, and it is added into the output word at ($5EFF). $7981 is where an entry of 0 jumps, adding nothing.

Moves the vertex before IX (IX-6, three words) along the edge from it to the vertex at IX until it lies on the clip plane $5EDB: 1 is x = -z, 2 is y = -z, 3 is x = z, 4 is y = z, and anything else the plane z = 0. The fraction of the edge is a ratio of differences, t1 / t2, and each coordinate moves by its own difference times t1 / t2 (mul_16x16 then div_32_16, rounded). On the planes x = +-z or y = +-z the coordinate on the plane is set from the new z.

Says which side of the clip plane $5EDB the vertex at IX is on: A = 0 inside, 1 outside, $FF on the plane. Planes 1 and 2 test x + z and y + z, 3 and 4 test z - x and z - y, anything else z itself; outside is a negative word (by its sign bit).

Projects the $8A7F turned vertices at $5E9F onto the view, two bytes each at $8A6B: x' = cx + x x cx / z and y' = cy + y x cy / z, with cx and cy the view's half-width and half-height ($88D9, $88DA), by mul_16x8 and div_24_16. A coordinate outside the view's pyramid is clamped to 0 or to twice the half-size, and a vertex at z = 0 goes to the centre.

Turns the $8A7F vertices at $5E63 through the view (rotate_vertices), then tests them against the clip planes from $8A80 down to 1 (clip_classify). $5E5F is 0 if every vertex is outside some plane, so nothing of them can be seen, and 1 otherwise; $5E5E is 1 if some vertex was outside a plane tested, so the faces must be clipped.

Clips the polygon of $8A7F turned vertices at $5E9F against each clip plane from $8A80 down to 1, Sutherland and Hodgman's way: the vertices' sides of the plane go to $5F40, and each edge that crosses it adds its crossing point (clip_edge) to the output at $5F03, each vertex inside adding itself, a point the same as the last one added left out ($5F3F counts them). A polygon of more than two corners closes on its first vertex, copied after its last. What is left goes back to $5E9F and $8A7F; fewer than two corners leave $8A7F = 0, and so does a polygon with no vertex inside a plane.

Says which way round the three screen points at HL go, by the side of the line through the first two that the third is on: A = 0 or 1, and 1 when they are in a line. Points in a vertical or a horizontal line are decided by comparisons; otherwise the line's slope is worked out x 2048 (div_24_16), with x and y of all three swapped first when the line is steep (and swapped back after), and the third point's height against the line's at its x gives the side.
Masks of the left 1 to 7 pixels of a byte, then of single pixels 1 to 7, for fill_face's partial bytes.

Fills a face from the span table ($8A9F, three bytes a row: 0, 1 or 2 ends set, and their x) into the view buffer, from row $8919 down to row $891B, in the pattern of colour $8917: four bytes a colour from ($891D), one for each row modulo 4. Rows are stored bottom up, ($88DD) bytes each, from ($8A95). A row with one end set is a single pixel; x counts from 1, so a span starting at 0 loses that pixel. Each row's ends are cleared as it is filled.

Puts the faces of an object, at IY, into the face list at ($8BDC), when every corner is inside the clip planes: the corners are projected (project_vertices), and each face of the list (a colour byte and a corner count, then the corners' numbers) gets a byte, its colour x 16 plus its count, then its corners' screen points. A face of colour 0 is skipped. With $5E60 = 1 only faces whose corners go one way round (face_side) are kept; with 2 the side seen picks the colour from the nibbles of $8917. When any face was kept the object goes into the draw list ($8BE0: where its faces are, and where its corners are in the object buffer), the face list and the object buffer (12 bytes) move on, and $8918 counts it.

Puts the faces of an object, at IY, into the face list when some corner is outside a clip plane: each face's corners are copied to $5E9F, clipped (clip_polygon), projected and kept or skipped as draw_face_list does. A face of four corners left at the four corners of the view fills it: it ends the object, $8A6A counts it and bit 7 of the object's face count marks it, so draw_faces can start there.
Does the face fill the whole view: its four points at (0, 0), (0, 2cy), (2cx, 2cy) and (2cx, 0) in any order?
prepare_polygon's two lengths of the edge it is stepping along.

Turns the $8A7F screen corners at IX of a polygon into the span table at ($8A9F), three bytes a row: the corners are copied to $8A6B with the first again after the last, $8919 and $891B take the highest and the lowest row, and each edge in turn sets, on every row it crosses from its top end down, one end of the row's span (the first x a row gets, then a second if it differs). A level edge on the top or bottom row sets both ends at once. A steep edge steps a row at a time and moves x when its error passes; a shallow one steps x until its error passes and keeps the first x of each row. IX is left after the corners.
prepare_line's two lengths of the line it is stepping along.

Turns the line of two screen points at IX into the span table: every row from the top end to the bottom one gets the x the line is at (one end set), and a shallow line a span from where it enters a row to where it leaves; $8919 and $891B take its rows. IX is left after the points.
Multiplies HL by A, both signed, into A:H:L, a signed 24-bit product: the magnitudes by shift and add from the top set bit of A, then the sign. A or HL of 0 gives 0 at once. BC and DE are kept.

Multiplies HL by DE, both signed, into DE:HL, a signed 32-bit product: the magnitudes by shift and add, the multiplier's bits taken from its top set one, then the sign. HL of 0 clears DE, DE of 0 clears HL. AF and BC are kept.
The sign of div_24_16's quotient (1 or $FF), and the count of bits left to divide.

Divides A:H:L by DE, both signed, into A:H:L, the quotient truncated towards zero, with DE the remainder of the two magnitudes. The dividend is shifted up to its top set bit, then divided a bit at a time by restoring subtraction for the bits that are left ($91F0). A dividend of 0 gives 0 and DE = 0.
Multiplies H by L, both signed bytes, into HL. Either of 0 gives 0 at once. AF, BC and DE are kept.
The sign of div_32_16's quotient (1 or $FF), and its running remainder, a word.

Divides DE:HL by BC, both signed, into DE:HL, with BC the remainder of the magnitudes (also at $92D5). The quotient of the magnitudes is rounded up when the remainder less half the divisor is not negative, then given its sign: so it is the nearest whole number, halves away from zero. A dividend of 0 gives 0 and BC = 0. AF is kept.
The last bit, then the rounding: the remainder against half the divisor.

Writes the number DE:HL in decimal as A ASCII digits ending at IX + A - 1, leading zeros kept: each digit is the remainder of a division by 10 (div_32_16), whose rounding of the quotient is undone when the remainder is 5 or more. Every register is kept.

Prints the text at IX on the screen. HL points at a record: the screen address (a word) and the number of characters. Each character is six bytes of the font that $8A81 points to, from character $20 on, written to six pixel rows of a cell, one under the other ($100 apart). Every register is kept.
